title: prefill-decode: overlap stages and speculative chunked prefill to reduce tail latency
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: prefill (encoder/prefix) and decode (autoregressive) stages have historically been executed sequentially which increases end-to-end p99/p999 latency for mixed prefill+decode requests. This PR implements three complementary optimizations to improve tail latency and throughput: (1) chunked prefill (speculative prefill) that emits KV cache chunks earlier and allows the decode stage to start on partial prefixes, (2) stage overlap where prefill and decode run on separate execution lanes and synchronize via well-defined chunk handoff, and (3) scheduler hints + kernel adjustment to prioritize short-decode requests and reduce head-of-line blocking. Changes also include KV cache coherence adjustments and safety checks to keep outputs identical to baseline deterministic runs. Results: microbenchmarks show 12-28% reduction in p99 latency and 6-18% higher sustained throughput on mixed prefill/decode workloads (batch sizes and seq lengths representative of production traces). Canary on perf-canary cluster validated tail latency improvement and no quality regressions on eval prompts. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf benchmarks and canary - [x] Docs and knobs for tuning - [x] Rollout plan (canary->gradual traffic) Main user-visible behavior: no API changes. Changes are opt-in behind runtime config flags initially and will be enabled by default after canary validation. Backwards compatibility: KV cache on-disk format unchanged; in-memory chunk accounting added but does not persist across restarts. See release notes for rollout guidance and tuning knobs.
commits_summary: feat(prefill): implement chunked/speculative prefill emitter and chunked KV cache API
perf(scheduler): add stage overlap runner and lane-based execution
core(runtime): synchronized chunk handoff and safety fences between prefill and decode
kv: add chunk accounting and partial-kv read path
bench: add mixed prefill-decode harness and baseline comparison
docs: add prefill-decode performance guide and rollout notes
tests: add unit tests for chunking boundary cases and integration perf smoke
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Overall this looks promising. Can you double-check the memory accounting under high-concurrency to avoid unbounded growth? Also add a toggle at the lane-level to disable overlap for degenerate workloads.

Maya Chen: Addressed. Added per-lane soft-cap and eviction policy; updated runtime_flags.yaml to include lane.disable_overlap and lane.max_chunked_prefill_memory. Added unit tests for eviction behavior.
Priya Singh: The kernel selection change looks risky for older GPU families. Did you run validation on our smallest nodes?

Maya Chen: Yes — added a fallback path that uses the baseline kernel selection for legacy SMs. Included automated canary config to avoid scheduling overlapped lanes on legacy nodes until further validation.

Diego Alvarez: Two small nits: 1) move the handoff metrics into the per-route counters; 2) add a short doc blurb describing when speculative prefill may increase compute cost for very short-lived sessions.
Maya Chen: Fixed both. Handoff metrics are now emitted as route.handoff.* and docs updated with cost tradeoffs and tuning knobs.
ci_checks: Perf regression: pass (improved on mixed workloads)
benchmarks_summary: Mixed workload (prefill+decode) p99 latency: baseline 312ms -> now 243ms (22% improvement)
Sustained throughput: +6-18% depending on batch shape and sequence distribution
CPU/GPU utilization: improved pipeline balance, decode lanes less frequently starved
Memory: per-lane soft-cap prevented >6% increase in peak RSS in high-concurrency scenarios
canary_notes: Deployed to perf-canary cluster (subset of nodes) for 48h
No correctness/quality regressions observed on open-eval prompt set
Observed ~15% p99 improvement on production-like traces; rollout configured to 10% traffic then 50% after 24h
Rollback plan: toggle runtime_flags.disable_prefill_overlap or revert lane assignment via router policy
release_notes: Introduces chunked/speculative prefill and stage-overlap execution to reduce p99/p999 latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads. Opt-in via runtime flags; default enabling subject to canary validation. See docs/perf/prefill_decode_optimizations.md for tuning and rollout guidance.
merge_commit_message: squash: prefill-decode stage overlap and speculative chunked prefill (perf improvements)
notes: Opt-in runtime flags: runtime_flags.yaml entries added; operators should monitor route.handoff.latency and route.handoff.pending_chunks
Follow-ups planned: autotuning heuristics to dynamically adjust chunk size and lane priorities (ENG-4920), support for multi-model shared-KV caches
Security: no user data leak risk introduced; KV cache chunking remains scoped to same-request isolation boundaries
